title: Pull Requests and Code Review
description: Practice pull requests and code review through a concrete team scenario.

blocks.content: A **pull request (PR)** is a proposal to merge one branch into another. It's how teams review code before it reaches the main branch. Pull requests aren't a Git feature per se - they're provided by hosting platforms like GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket. But they're central to how almost every team works.

## The Pull Request Flow

```
1. Push your feature branch to the remote
   git push origin feature/my-thing

2. Go to GitHub (or your platform) and open a Pull Request
   - Select your branch as the source
   - Select main as the destination
   - Write a description of what changed and why

3. Teammates review the code
   - They can leave comments on specific lines
   - Request changes or approve

4. Address feedback with new commits on the same branch
   git add .
   git commit -m "address review feedback"
   git push origin feature/my-thing

5. Once approved, merge via the platform UI (or git merge locally)

6. Delete the branch - it has served its purpose
```

## What Makes a Good PR

- **Small and focused** - one feature or fix, not everything you've done this week
- **Clear description** - explain what it does and why, link to any relevant issue
- **Tests pass** - don't ask people to review broken code
- **Self-review first** - read through your own diff before requesting review

## Keeping Your Branch Up to Date

While your PR is in review, main may have gotten new commits. Update your branch:
```
git switch feature/my-thing
git pull origin main
```

Or with rebase for a cleaner history:
```
git rebase main
```

blocks.question: What is the main purpose of a pull request?
options: To automatically deploy the code to production
To give the team a place to review and discuss changes before they merge into main
To pull the latest changes from the remote
To request that someone else finishes your work
blocks.explanation: A pull request is a review mechanism. It shows the team exactly what changed, gives everyone a place to comment on specific lines of code, and creates a record of the discussion. The code only merges after the team is satisfied.

blocks.prompt: Fetch the latest changes from origin and merge them into the current branch.
